title: Degenerated differential pair
description: A source-degenerated differential pair: a resistor $R_s$ in each source lifts the linear input range and improves offset at the cost of transconductance. The effective transconductance is $G_m = g_m/(1 + g_m*R_s)$; the degeneration factor $n_{deg} = 1 + g_m*R_s$ divides GBW and the input offset while the ~1-decade linear range extends to about $V^* + (I_{tail}/2)*R_s$. The bind declares $V_{SB} = (I_{tail}/2)*R_s$ to record the source lift the degeneration introduces (inert on a table with no body-effect axis, a real slice on one that has it). Degeneration's boost of the device output resistance is neglected here, so the gain into a fixed load conductance is a conservative estimate.

params.name: linrange_target
params.note: required single-ended linear input range (differential is roughly twice this)

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget, including the degeneration resistor

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input CM at which the operating point is evaluated

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: drain DC level; sets the input device vds

params.name: R_s
params.note: per-side degeneration resistance; gm*R_s sets the linearization and offset improvement

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion; high gm/ID makes degeneration more effective (larger gm*R_s)

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs, used to place the input drain node; retune until input-bias-consistent is green

doc.title: Input-pair device (degenerated)
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, with R_s in its source. vsb records the source lift the degeneration introduces.

params.name: vsb_i
params.note: source-bulk lift from the degeneration resistor, (I_tail/2)*R_s

rows.name: n_deg
rows.note: degeneration factor; Gm, GBW, and vos all scale by 1/n_deg

rows.name: Av
rows.note: conservative: neglects the degeneration boost of the device output resistance

rows.name: vos_undeg
rows.note: the un-degenerated Pelgrom offset of the input pair

rows.name: vos
rows.note: degeneration divides the offset by n_deg (the gm-mismatch term is linearized away)

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: device density plus the degeneration resistor's 4kT*R_s, both sides of the pair (estimate)

rules.note: degeneration must extend the linear range to the target
the input drain node placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
